{{Short description|Special kind of model structure}}
In [[higher category theory]] in [[mathematics]], a '''Cisinski model structure''' is a special kind of [[model structure]] on [[Grothendieck topos|Grothendieck topoi]]. In homotopical algebra, the [[category of simplicial sets]] is of particular interest. Cisinski model structures are named after [[Denis-Charles Cisinski]], who introduced them in 2001. His work is based on unfinished ideas presented by Alexander Grothendieck in his script ''[[Pursuing Stacks]]'' from 1983.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Grothendieck |date= |title=Pursuing Stacks |url=https://thescrivener.github.io/PursuingStacks/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200730015735/https://thescrivener.github.io/PursuingStacks/ps-online.pdf |archive-date=30 Jul 2020 |access-date=2020-09-17 |website=thescrivener.github.io}}</ref>

== Definition ==
A cofibrantly generated model structure on a topos, for the cofibrations are exactly the monomorphisms, is called a ''Cisinski model structure''. Cofibrantly generated means that there are small sets <math>I</math> and <math>J</math> of morphisms, on which the [[small object argument]] can be applied, so that they generate all cofibrations and trivial cofibrations using the [[lifting property]]:<ref>Cisinski 2019, 2.4.1.</ref>

: <math>\operatorname{Cofib}
={}^\perp(I^\perp);</math>
: <math>W\cap\operatorname{Cofib}
={}^\perp(J^\perp);</math>

More generally, a small set generating the class of monomorphisms of a category of [[presheaves]] is called ''cellular model'':<ref>Cisinski 2002, Définition 1.28.</ref><ref>Cisinski 2019, Definition 2.4.4.</ref>

: <math>\operatorname{Mono}
={}^\perp(I^\perp).</math>

Every topos admits a cellular model.<ref>Cisinski 2002, Proposition 1.29.</ref>

== Examples ==

* [[Joyal model structure]]: Cofibrations (monomorphisms) are generated by the boundary inclusions <math>\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n</math> and acyclic cofibrations (inner anodyne extensions) are generated by inner horn inclusions <math>\Lambda_k^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n</math> (with <math>n\geq 2</math> and <math>0<k<n</math>).<ref name=":2">Cisinski 2019, Example 2.4.5.</ref><ref>Cisinski 2019, Definition 3.2.1.</ref>
* [[Kan–Quillen model structure]]: Cofibrations (monomorphisms) are generated by the boundary inclusions <math>\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n</math> and acyclic cofibrations (anodyne extensions) are generated by horn inclusions <math>\Lambda_k^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n</math> (with <math>n\geq 2</math> and <math>0\leq k\leq n</math>).<ref name=":2" />
